episodes.193546: A line of thunderstorms moved through the Nebraska Panhandle the afternoon of 23 August. Bowing segments in the line produced strong downburst winds across Scotts Bluff and Kimball Counties as the line progressed eastward.
episodes.193814: A cluster of strong thunderstorms and an outflow boundary moved from east to west across the area with measured wind gusts in excess of 34 knots and one report of a waterspout offshore of St George Island.
episodes.194046: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms brought severe wind gusts to eastern Weld and Logan Counties.
episodes.194117: A surface low meandered offshore of the NE FL coastal along a stalled front. Passing upper-level short wave trough energy, high moisture and slow storm motion produced locally heavy rainfall and pulse strong storms with wet downbursts in resultant storms. Storms impacted coastal areas in the morning, then with diurnal heating shift inland.

episodes.194252: An anomalously strong upper level trough was set up just off the west coast, which resulted in a strong belt of mid level southerly flow across Southwest through North-central Montana. Synoptic winds were already breezy from the south, allowing thunderstorms to easily produce strong wind gusts given inverted-V soundings. Wind gusts in excess of 80 mph were observed on this day as a line of gusty outflow spread northward over the plains.||A High Wind Warning was also issued for Southwest Montana this day, though no strong synoptic gusts were observed.
episodes.194435: Despite being beneath a strong upper high-pressure center, scattered diurnal convection developed across northwestern Oklahoma. Strong heating and weak wind shear promoted a few disorganized storms with reports of downburst wind damage.
episodes.194450: Several severe thunderstorms causing significant wind damage in the Bitterroot, Mission, and Seeley-Swan valleys.
episodes.195109: Thunderstorm activity developed across much of eastern AZ, along the higher terrain features, during the early afternoon hours. Outflow boundaries emanating from the activity over the higher terrain areas sparked a complex of robust thunderstorms over Pinal County. A northwestward moving outflow boundary that developed from the Pinal County storms produced wind gusts in excess of 50 mph as well as areas of dense blowing dust across the Phoenix East Valley. Additional thunderstorm activity then developed over central Phoenix during the late afternoon, likely instigated by a convergence zone that set up right over the area with little convective inhibition in place and thus it did not take much of a triggering mechanism to get convective initiation. With MLCAPE values of 1000-1500 J/KG along with DCAPE of around 1500 J/KG, conditions were favorable for the generation of strong to severe downburst winds.
episodes.195345: Isolated severe thunderstorms produced wind damage mainly across portions of Callahan and Taylor counties.
episodes.195406: A surface high pressure centered over the central Atlantic Ocean induced an easterly wind flow. The easterly winds interacting with Vieques promoted the formation of a fair-weather waterspout downwind from the islands.
episodes.195490: With deep monsoonal moisture in place, as well as around 1000 J/kg of instability and some bulk shear aloft, widespread strong to severe thunderstorms formed across the Four Corners region. This resulted in multiple severe threats in eastern Utah which included large hail and flash flooding due to heavy rainfall rates in excess of 2 inches per hour.
episodes.195768: Modest instability and a sharpening coastal trough along the western portion of the Gulf Stream led to showers and thunderstorms capable of producing damaging wind gusts across South Carolina coastal waters.
episodes.195897: Severe thunderstorms rolled through portions of the Tucson Metro resulting in strong winds and localized hail.
episodes.195991: In the afternoon of the 22nd, a boundary along Interstate 70 that was slowly moving south fired multiple thunderstorms. These initial storms began to cluster together near Burlington and produce extensive wind damage and two tornadoes that caused no damage. Hail up to 1.75 inches was also reported.
episodes.195992: In the late afternoon of the 22nd, a cluster of storms in eastern Colorado began forming into a line of storms as it entered western Kansas in the early evening. Penny sized hail and a wind gust up to 70 MPH were recorded from these storms.
episodes.196079: An active upper level pattern with a series of shortwave troughs moving over the region throughout the course of the week produced several days of strong to severe thunderstorms over the region.
episodes.196104: Reports of trees downed with damage.
episodes.196111: Very strong winds were observed during a widespread outbreak of severe weather.
episodes.196146: There were gusty winds for different parts of Utah and flash flooding in southern Utah.
episodes.196239: Several gale-force wind gusts were observed over the Florida Keys coastal waters as a tropical wave moved westward.
episodes.196301: A collapsing thunderstorm produced a small downburst in Young County that damaged trees, broke power poles, and blew a car off the road.
episodes.196346: Afternoon thunderstorms south of a stalled out frontal boundary over the north-central Florida peninsula produce wind damage near Saint Leo in Pasco County when a tree falls onto a home.
